correctness.rationale: For any missing edge uv, exact operator-norm Cauchy bound yields ||P-J|| >=1/(n-1). Equality forces H(e_v-1/n)=-(1/(n-1))(e_u-1/n), so a vertex with two distinct nonneighbors is impossible. Conversely the explicit matching-deleted kernel is nonnegative and stochastic; its four invariant subspace types have eigenvalues 1, +a, -a, 0 with a=1/(n-1), giving exact equality. Compactness makes the nonmatching case strictly larger. Reconstructable for all n>=3; standard-library rational checker replayed 224 pairs n<=30, and finite replay is not used as the proof.

originality.rationale: Compared previously available mathematical claims about graph/spectral mixing for overlap, multiple actual published-finding corpus semantic formulations, and 2004/2009 primary full texts plus accessible 2025 broader article. The edge-transitive perfect-matching subcase is already known and explicitly excluded from standalone novelty. The all-graphs iff matching-complement characterization with necessity from equality saturation and constructive partial-matching sufficiency was not implied by the inspected published theorems; general SDP techniques alone are not an exact statement. Residual risk that an overlooked more general dual theorem implies this consequence is explicitly retained.
residual_risks: An undiscovered or indirectly implied extremal equality theorem may occur in the extensive SDP-duality and stochastic-matrix completion literature; searchable results and inspected primary full text cannot prove global uniqueness.
The perfect-matching-deleted equal-value special case follows already from Boyd et al. (2009) edge-transitive theory and is not independently novel.
Other faster mixing definitions (total-variation time, nonreversible chains or forbidden holding loops) have distinct optima and are outside the claim.

value.rationale: The question seeks the optimal *resilience of uniform mixing to missing communication links* across all finite graph topologies, not an arbitrary small graph instance. The result gives the globally sharp minimum nonzero spectral mixing obstruction on every noncomplete n-vertex support and a complete graph-theoretic characterization of equality. It distinguishes vertex-disjoint link failures, whose optimal penalty never worsens, from shared-endpoint failures, which strictly worsen it; this is a structural design principle for link-failure patterns. The full iff theorem is strictly more informative than a known single-family SLEM formula or one computed table.
